parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the parent's Feb-2025 document/entry regime (X markers barred, refusal where sex is doubted, possible lifetime fraud finding, reported passport confiscation/stranding, eight-plus foreign travel advisories), federal exclusion from government single-sex facilities, and documented immigration-custody abuse (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse) are traveller-facing exposures no state protection reaches. The division counters with enforced anti-discrimination (July 2026 conviction), hate-crime enhancements, abolished trans-panic defence, a 2024 ruling protecting trans students, and 88% public support. No division facility ban or criminalisation is documented. Litigation is unresolved, so exposure varies by travel date. Severity is entry refusal, stranding and possible custody abuse — not imprisonment for identity itself, no execution risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 EO and foreign-ministry cable: X markers barred, cases refused where discrepancy casts doubt on sex, fraud ground considered for wilful misrepresentation (possible lifetime ineligibility). Travellers report passports confiscated/blocked and stranding; eight-plus foreign governments issued advisories for trans citizens.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding is never automatic (four elements, limited waivers); civil-liberties union suit pending; some measures enjoined elsewhere.
entry_documents.interaction: Border control is federal — division protections never reach it; document discrepancy can cascade into refusal, detention and custody placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Transgender men in immigration custody reportedly subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. Corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates from 2026 (hair, hormones, psychiatric drugs) and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers. Trespass bathroom arrest documented in another division.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute; several executive orders blocked or enjoined; division courts have ruled for trans people (Aug 2024).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document doubt can move a visitor from the border directly into the federal custody system where the documented abuse occurs.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal EO bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity (applies inside this division). Nationally 9+1 divisions ban all-government-building access, 6 reach private settings, 4 criminalise in circumstances; one documented arrest elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No facility ban documented for this division; division high court protected trans students (Aug 2024); division anti-discrimination covers public accommodations since 2018/2020.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule overrides division tolerance in federal buildings; division ban status itself is not documented.

care_services.exposure: Division banned gender-affirming medicine for minors (2024) and, from Jan 2026, blockers, hormones and chest surgery for under-18s, with provider discipline and a right to sue; national EO frames such care as 'mutilation'. A minor traveller could be denied refills or continuation.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned in division; division anti-discrimination covers health care since 2020; grandfather clause for treatment underway by 1 Jan 2026; emergency care denial not documented.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor plus guardian meets division ban first, federal hostile framing and possible insurance rules second.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders and agency language ('chemical and surgical mutilation', 'radical gender ideology', counterterrorism priority on 'radically pro-transgender' groups); 66% national poll support for birth-sex document listing; 2025 census recorded 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in this division (raw count, second-highest, no denominator).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division poll: 88% support for discrimination protections (2022); trans-panic defence abolished 2024; DOJ-adjacent civil-rights enforcement documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing raises outing and scrutiny probability at every federal touchpoint regardless of division attitudes.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division care bans reach a travelling minor needing refills; sports ban requires birth certificate for eligibility; national EO directs law enforcement to prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition — resident-facing but signals official framing of trans minors as endangered.
minors_guardians.protection: Division Aug 2024 highest-court ruling protected transgender students on privacy/autonomy grounds; anti-bullying statute covers gender identity and expression; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2019.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces division care denial plus heightened national scrutiny; remedies operate at division level only.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents recorded in division for 2025 (raw count, second-highest nationally, no per-capita denominator — magnitude unclear); a man struck a transgender woman, showing such assaults occur.
street_violence_police_response.protection: County court found civil-rights violation and held attacker liable (July 2026); hate-crime penalty enhancements since 2019; trans-panic defence abolished; documented enforcement of the civil-rights statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State prosecution of an assailant shows police/courts work for trans people here, partially offsetting national hostility at street level.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and several executive orders unresolved; injunction status varies by date, so exposure changes with travel timing; care-ban injunction status unknown; incident census lacks denominator; 'least safe in region' label is attributed, not measured.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division civil-rights enforcement documented (2026 conviction, 2024 court ruling); legal-aid FAQ tracks passport rules; national hate-crime statute and equality litigation remain available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Division remedies cannot reach border, federal-facility or immigration-custody exposures; federal remedies are litigation-dependent and uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's anchor is routine discretionary entry exclusion with no arrest and no remedy. This dossier's border regime is comparably discretionary (refusal on sex doubt) but harsher in consequence — possible lifetime fraud finding, documented stranding, plus a custody-abuse pathway. It scores higher than 0.35-A because the division supplies enforced anti-discrimination, working courts for trans people, and no local criminalisation.

Drellia's anchor: registration, nightly hotel-to-database transmission, repeated officer interviews, slow unresponsive ombuds, charges uncommon. Similar in kind — durable exposure through documents and databases with weak remedy. This case rates about level: equivalent document-driven exposure and thin traveller recourse, but offset by division enforcement actually producing a conviction, while Drellia's anchor offers no such documented relief.

Kestrel Isles' anchor is secondary screening with administrative refusal, slow appeal, humiliation — but no custody abuse and no facility exclusion. This dossier is worse: refusal carries a possible permanent bar, stranding is documented, foreign governments warn their citizens, federal facility exclusion and immigration-custody abuse apply. Sits clearly below 0.55-B despite stronger division protections.

Meridia's anchor has trained border officers, brief detention, written reasons, counsel access, compensation — protections operating at the border itself. Here the border layer is hostile (refusal, fraud referral, confiscation reports) and federal custody has documented abuse. Far below 0.75-C; the division's good record cannot reach the entry and federal-custody stages.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters two layered systems. At the border and in federal buildings the parent regime is operative and hostile: document scrutiny with refusal and a possible lifetime fraud finding, reported passport confiscation and stranding, foreign-government advisories, exclusion from government single-sex facilities, and — if custody follows refusal — documented abuse in immigration detention. No division measure touches any of these; the division's enforced anti-discrimination, hate-crime enhancements, 2024 pro-trans student ruling and 88% public support operate only below that layer, where they genuinely work (2026 conviction). Within the division, everyday street exposure is moderate; a travelling minor additionally faces the division's 2026 care bans. Litigation keeps several federal measures in flux, so severity depends on travel date, but the entry document regime is in force.
